samples.summary: New §8.1 sentence overstates the contract: "Every command that renders a *result* routes it through `output()`" is not true of the branch. `sheets export` formats with `formatCsv`/`formatJson` and writes directly (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46-53), and `docs/notes/slides import` write their JSON result via `process.stdout.write` (packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:47, notes/import.ts:40, slides/import.ts:66). The parenthetical only excuses `login`/`logout`/`ctx switch`. A canonical design doc that overstates the invariant is worse than silence — narrow the claim to the session commands the issue actually covers.
samples.evidence: cli.md:710 "Every command that renders a *result* routes it through `output()`" vs sheets-export.ts:46 `const formatted = fmt === 'csv' ? formatCsv(res.data) : formatJson(res.data);`

samples.summary: The new `ctx list` exit-code rule contradicts the exit-code table four lines above it in the same section: cli.md:706-708 assigns `2` to "system error (network, auth)" and `1` to "user error (bad input, not found)". `NOT_LOGGED_IN` is an auth condition, yet the doc (and `outputError`, which hardcodes `process.exitCode = 1`) makes it exit 1. Either the table needs a carve-out saying "missing session is a user error" or the code should exit 2; as written §8.1 documents two incompatible answers for the same condition.
samples.evidence: cli.md:706 "`2` system error (network, auth)" vs cli.md:722 "emits ... `\"code\": \"NOT_LOGGED_IN\"` and exits `1`"; formatter.ts:87 `process.exitCode = 1;`

samples.summary: The not-logged-in message now exists in three places: `NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE` exported from status.ts:31, a hardcoded copy inside `NotLoggedInError` (ctx.ts:39), and a third literal in `ctx switch` (ctx.ts:95). The change deliberately exported the constant from `status.ts` yet did not reuse it one file over. Repo convention is reuse of shared strings/types; the copies will drift.
samples.evidence: status.ts:31 `export const NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE = 'Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.';` vs ctx.ts:39 `super('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.');` vs ctx.ts:95 `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.');`

samples.summary: Layering inconsistency: `InvalidFormatError` (with its structured `code`) was placed in the shared `output/formatter.ts`, but `NotLoggedInError` — a session-level condition that `ctx switch`, and any future session-dependent command, needs identically — is declared privately inside `ctx.ts`. A session error belongs next to `loadSession` (`src/config/session.ts`) or in the shared error surface, not in one command module.
samples.evidence: ctx.ts:34-41 `class NotLoggedInError extends Error { readonly code = 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'; ... }` (not exported) vs formatter.ts:14 `export class InvalidFormatError`

samples.summary: Validation is now performed twice on the same value: `format()` gained a throwing `default:` branch (formatter.ts:51-55) *and* ~25 command call sites each call `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` immediately before `output()`, which itself calls `format()`. Since every one of those call sites is already inside the same try/catch that would catch the throw from `output()`, the extra line is redundant boilerplate for all read-only commands; only the ordering-sensitive cases (e.g. `api-keys create`, which must fail before the key is minted) genuinely need the early call. Consider keeping the early call only where ordering matters, or validating once inside `output()`.
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:51-55 default branch throws InvalidFormatError; e.g. tabs.ts:18 `const fmt = parseOutputFormat(opts.format);` followed by tabs.ts:21 `output(res.data, fmt, opts.quiet);` inside one try/catch

samples.summary: An in-repo source comment is left asserting the very defect this PR fixes: it states `status` ignores `--format json` and prints prose, calls it "ground-truth defect #9", and justifies the module's whole approach on that basis. After this change the statement is false, so the rationale for not asking the CLI no longer holds. Not updating it leaves a stale ground-truth claim (mirrored in .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15-20) that will mislead the next reader.

samples.summary: `formatTable` now renders any single non-array object as a key/value table, changing `--format table` output for every command that emits one object (`docs get/create/rename/delete`, `schema`, `cells set`, …), which previously printed `(no results)`. This is beyond the issue's stated approach (which only asked for status/ctx list plus format validation) — justified as an enabler for `status --format table`, but it is an undisclosed cross-command output change worth calling out in the PR description and the docs page.

samples.summary: `ctx switch` still reports failures as bare prose on stderr and calls `process.exit(1)` rather than the structured `outputError` body, so §8.1's "Errors are also JSON so agents can parse success and failure uniformly" remains false for the sibling of the command this PR just fixed. finding.summary: New agent-facing error codes (`INVALID_FORMAT`, `NOT_LOGGED_IN`) are not added to §10 Error Matrix, the canonical table agents/skills read for codes
finding.evidence: The change introduces two new structured error codes: `InvalidFormatError.code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:15) and `NotLoggedInError.code = 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:36). §8.1 prose mentions them (docs/design/cli.md:722,725) but the canonical enumeration in §10 "Error Matrix" (lines 960-976, which lists INVALID_RANGE, FILE_EXISTS, INVALID_DOCX, etc. with exit codes) was left untouched. An agent reading the matrix to learn the code vocabulary will not find either code, nor the exit code (`ctx list` → 1) they imply.

verdict.reason:
The literal table-row omission is real, but the documentation obligation it claims is unmet is already discharged in the canonical design doc, and the finding's premise about §10 is false.

1) Both new codes ARE documented in the canonical subsystem doc, in the section immediately preceding the matrix: docs/design/cli.md:721-722 states "`ctx list` cannot answer without a session, so it emits the standard error body with `\"code\": \"NOT_LOGGED_IN\"` and exits `1`" — so even the reviewer's specific sub-claim that "nor the exit code (`ctx list` → 1)" is documented is contradicted by the file. docs/design/cli.md:724-728 documents `INVALID_FORMAT` plus the rationale for per-command validation. So there is no missing/parallel design doc: the canonical `docs/design/cli.md` was folded into, exactly as CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline requires, and the originating task's acceptance item "`docs/design/cli.md` prose references updated" (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:96) is satisfied.

2) §10 "Error Matrix" (docs/design/cli.md:960-976) is demonstrably NOT the exhaustive canonical vocabulary the finding asserts. Multiple pre-existing, in-use CLI error codes are absent from it: `INVALID_PPTX` (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-import.ts:61), `SESSION_EXPIRED` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:132), `HTTP_ERROR` / `INVALID_RESPONSE` (packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:164,201), and even `NOT_FOUND` (packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:28) which appears only in the §8.1 example at docs/design/cli.md:699. Per-command codes are documented in skills instead (packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:80) and the README states codes are "command-specific" (packages/cli/README.md:109-113). Nothing in CONTRIBUTING.md imposes a rule that every new code must be added to that table.

Given the codes, messages and exit codes are documented in the canonical doc, adding two more rows to a table that already omits five other live codes is a documentation-tidiness preference (minor/nit under this rubric: "could be cleaner"), not a failed acceptance criterion, missing design doc, duplication, or Non-Goal breach. It should not gate the merge.

finding.summary: §8.1 now promises `INVALID_FORMAT` for any unsupported `--format`, but the content/export commands it explicitly names still emit code `ERROR`
finding.evidence: The added prose reads: "An unsupported `--format` value is rejected with `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` rather than ignored. Validation is per-command because `docs`/`slides`/`notes` `content` and `export` deliberately reuse the same global `--format` flag …". That sentence tells an agent those commands also report INVALID_FORMAT, but `parseContentFormat` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:27) throws a plain `Error`, so `outputError`'s `errorCode()` falls back to `'ERROR'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75). The same holds for `detectExportFormat` in packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39 and the slides/notes equivalents. Either those validators should carry `code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` or the doc should scope the claim to `output()` commands only.

verdict.reason: The quoted prose exists verbatim at docs/design/cli.md:724-728 and explicitly names `docs`/`slides`/`notes` `content` and `export` in the same paragraph that promises `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` for an unsupported `--format`, with no scoping to `output()` commands. Only `InvalidFormatError` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:14-22) carries that code; `errorCode()` (formatter.ts:70-76) flattens anything else to `'ERROR'`. The named per-command validators all throw plain `Error`: parseContentFormat (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:25-32), detectExportFormat (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39-54), and the slides/notes equivalents (packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:26, packages/cli/src/notes/content.ts:10, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:202, packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:195). The originating task scoped the new code to `output()` callers (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:21-29; lessons file:11-14), so the updated design doc overstates implemented behavior for the commands it names. No guard re-codes those errors, so the divergence is real and stands as a design-doc/implementation conformance defect in this lens's lane.
